topic: Nobel Prize Winners: India and the World
description: A comprehensive exam-oriented study guide covering the history of the Nobel Prize, distinguished Indian laureates, and significant global records, including firsts and multiple-time winners.

sections.title: Introduction to the Nobel Prize
sections.description: Fundamental facts and history about the world's most prestigious award.

key_concepts.explanation: An international award established by the will of Swedish scientist and inventor Alfred Nobel in 1895. It is awarded to those who have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind.
Originally, it was awarded in 5 categories: Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, and Peace. The prize for Economic Sciences was added later.

historical_events.significance: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded five years after Alfred Nobel's death.

historical_events.event: Establishment of the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
historical_events.significance: Established by Sweden's central bank (Sveriges Riksbank) in memory of Alfred Nobel. It was first awarded in 1969.

important_facts.fact: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway, while all the other Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm, Sweden.
According to the statutes modified in 1974, a Nobel Prize cannot be awarded posthumously unless death occurs after the announcement of the prize.

sections.title: World's First and Unique Laureates
sections.description: Crucial historical records and notable firsts in the history of the Nobel Prize.

important_facts.fact: The first woman to win a Nobel Prize was Marie Curie (Physics, 1903).
The youngest Nobel laureate in history is Malala Yousafzai, who won the Peace Prize in 2014 at the age of 17.
The youngest scientific Nobel laureate is Lawrence Bragg, who won the Physics Prize in 1915 at the age of 25.
The oldest person to be awarded a Nobel Prize is John B. Goodenough, who received the Chemistry Prize in 2019 at the age of 97.
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize the most times, winning it thrice (1917, 1944, and 1963).

sections.title: Individuals with Multiple Nobel Prizes
sections.description: Only an elite group of scientists and organizations have received the Nobel Prize more than once.
